plan.title: "How much progress have I made?" traces the path from the start

context.text: Hey Dana! 15 pages of Atomic Habits on the couch at 8.

transcript.text: Nice, Dana, 15 pages is a solid night. Real proof keeps it honest, so send me a photo of the page you stopped on and I'll log it.
honestly how much progress have I actually made since I started with you?

Real progress, Dana. Here's what I've got:

• You started on Oct 13 at 5 pages a night, after not reading a book in two years.
• You got through your first full week with seven nights and no misses.
• You moved up to 10 pages on Oct 21, then to 15 on Oct 29 because 10 felt easy.
• You've done every step day since the 29th. One was the reduced version, and the rest were full.

You also switched from fighting your phone in bed to reading instead, and you've stuck with it. That's a real change. 📚

Send me the photo of the page you stopped on tonight and I'll log your 15 pages.

checks.reason: Only states the 15 pages and the tester's own done report; nothing invented.
Not applicable here; the text makes no claims about what ZOH knows about her.
Brings back the Oct 13 start from over a week earlier, woven into the progress list without reciting it.
Dates, page counts, the reduced day, and the first-week streak all match the memory pages.

conversation.reason: Today's 'done' is treated as done and the proof ask is light; the reduced day is correctly described as done, not missed.
Traces 5, 10, 15 pages accurately from Oct 13, but never names the original sleep goal, only the switch from bedtime.
Traces the path accurately with no invented facts and mentions recent done days, but omits the bedtime-goal start and runs longer than a short text or two.

grade.summary: ZOH traced the reading progress accurately from October 13 through the 5, 10 and 15 page steps, and mentioned the recent done days, including the one reduced day, without inventing anything. Its main gap is that it did not name the original bedtime goal as the true starting point, and the answer ran longer than the requested short text or two.
